stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features new support via Ollama's MLX engine, including native DFlash and image input.

stories.title: FTC alleges Amazon illegally made $20 billion by rigging billions of ad auctions
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The FTC has filed allegations against Amazon regarding its advertising practices.
The core accusation is that Amazon illegally manipulated ad auctions to inflate prices.
The FTC claims Amazon replaced actual auction results with higher prices it set.

stories.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
stories.author: Yeying Jin
bullet_points: H3-World is a new framework designed to transform large video generators (like MiniMax-H3) into interactive world models.
The research highlights that natural language is becoming a primary and effective interface for controlling increasingly capable large video generation models.
H3-World refines the existing coarse language control into precise, temporally grounded world control.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, standard in modern NLP/LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is relevant for text-generation tasks.
Categorizes the model under key ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to transformers, Llama architectures, and the AI community.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, enabling multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Google needs Hollywood more than the studios need AI
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Google is actively seeking licensing agreements with major Hollywood studios.
The goal is to train Google's AI models using copyrighted studio material.
Studios are reportedly being offered substantial financial compensation for these data rights.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and says it’s up to 45 percent cheaper for agentic work
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Anthropic released new models, Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, addressing prior customer concerns.
Fable 5.1 offers improved performance over Fable 5 while significantly reducing operational costs.
The new models boast substantial cost savings, up to 45% cheaper for complex agentic tasks.

stories.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Sambit Sahu
bullet_points: Introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) as a paradigm where natural language serves as a primary feedback mechanism for improving language agents.
VRL allows language models to receive feedback conveying intent, preferences, and causal structure in a human-interpretable format.
The field is structured around two axes: when verbal feedback is applied in an agent's lifecycle and what aspects of the agent it modifies.

stories.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
stories.author: Ziwei Wang
bullet_points: Facet-0 is a new robotic foundation model designed for high-precision, contact-rich manipulation tasks.
It integrates multimodal representation learning with reinforcement learning to predict and value contact consequences.
The model unifies causal wrench history with vision-language semantics and kinematic state for robust action planning.

stories.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
stories.author: Shekar Ramachandran
bullet_points: Investigates the uneven accuracy cost of Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Proposes a method to strategically allocate a limited additional precision budget to mitigate quantization damage.
Uses causal mixed-precision intervention across 9 open-weight models to test hypotheses on damage localization.

stories.title: NashDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Viliam Lisý
bullet_points: Introduces NashDreamer, a novel Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL) approach.
Addresses the significant challenge of applying MBRL to competitive, imperfect-information games (IIGs).
Argues for the necessity of centralized model learning to overcome non-stationarity and identifiability issues in multi-agent settings.

stories.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
stories.author: Shekar Ramachandran
bullet_points: The research investigates the uneven accuracy cost associated with Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
It proposes a method to intelligently allocate a limited additional precision budget by studying where quantization damage occurs.
The study validates hypotheses across 9 open-weight models and 4 architecture families using causal mixed-precision intervention as a ground truth.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon.
This allows Ollama to support a broader range of models across diverse hardware configurations.

stories.title: Acer’s new concept hardware is a gaming handheld with a keyboard
stories.author: Dominic Preston
bullet_points: Acer has unveiled a concept gaming handheld called Project DualPlay Mini.
The device aims to bridge the gap between bulky gaming laptops and smaller, less versatile handhelds.
It features a keyboard, suggesting a focus on enhanced PC gaming portability.

stories.title: Microsoft is enabling a Windows 11 security feature that can hurt gaming performance
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is expanding the rollout of the Windows 11 memory integrity security feature.
This kernel-level protection aims to prevent malicious code and drivers from running on the system.
A known side effect of the feature is a potential negative impact on PC gaming performance.

stories.title: It turns out that Orion's much-maligned heat shield performed really well
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Orion's heat shield has been validated as performing effectively, contrary to previous negative assessments.
Independent safety officials have provided positive feedback regarding recent leadership changes within NASA.
The story addresses a critical aspect of space exploration hardware performance and organizational oversight.

stories.title: Without new landers or rovers, it's helicopters or bust for NASA's Mars program
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: NASA's Mars program relies on helicopters as a potential means of surface mobility.
The SR-1 Freedom project has a base cost estimate of $2.1 billion, excluding helicopter costs.
The reliance on helicopters suggests a potential shift or constraint in future Mars mission design.

stories.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of evaluating AI software engineering agents on complex tasks.
Introduces PTA-IRT, a new framework that moves beyond simple pass/fail metrics to analyze *how* agents solve problems.
Leverages Trajectory-Aware Item Response Theory to provide a more nuanced and efficient performance evaluation.

stories.title: Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of repository-level code generation where context exceeds LLM input limits.
Proposes an 'Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval' method to improve context provision.
Highlights a limitation in existing RAG approaches: they often provide task-level support without explicit context identification.

stories.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
stories.author: Dimitri Kachler
bullet_points: Introduces CordisBench, a new 1,200-question benchmark designed to test language models' reasoning capabilities.
The benchmark focuses on the complex lifecycle reasoning required when language models dynamically alter their own execution environments (dynamic agent harnesses).
It addresses the challenge of tracking how local component changes propagate through dependencies and cleanup processes in complex software systems.

stories.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
stories.author: Stephen Morris
bullet_points: Presents a framework for mechanism design specifically tailored for AI agents with unknown preferences and capabilities.
The core challenge addressed is incentivizing AI agents to be both honest and obedient when acting on behalf of a designer.
The research establishes a 'revelation principle' using a one-sided imitation structure, characterizing implementable policies.

stories.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
stories.author: Chin-Chia Hsu
bullet_points: The research focuses on developing 'proactive thought partners' for writing, moving beyond simple autocomplete.
These AI agents aim to provide customizable, higher-level cognitive support tailored to the writer's needs at specific moments.
The paper explores the design space for AI that assists with diverse writing activities, from ideation to revision.

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by proposing a framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal allocation ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
stories.author: Bernardo Magnini
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost and brittleness of using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) directly for autonomous decision-making.
Introduces SAGE (Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy) to learn a cheap, autonomous policy from an imperfect VLM teacher.
The core mechanism involves querying the VLM only when the learning agent exhibits uncertainty.

stories.title: From Confusion to Clarity: Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection for Text Classification
stories.author: Jayasimha Talur
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation of LLMs in classifying text into taxonomies with highly similar, domain-specific labels.
Critiques the standard top-K retrieval method, noting it narrows candidates but fails to help the model differentiate between similar options.
Proposes a 'Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection' method to improve classification accuracy in complex label spaces.

stories.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
stories.author: Ming Jiang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the internal, poorly understood mechanisms of LLM-as-a-Judge systems used for evaluating Natural Language Generation (NLG) quality.
It employs an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy to mechanistically probe how LLMs assign ratings across Readability and Adequacy dimensions.
The research focuses on generating paired clean and corrupt summaries with controlled error intensity to test evaluator robustness.

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally allocating a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations by developing a principled framework to characterize near-optimal SFT-RL allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal SFT-RL ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
stories.author: Bernardo Magnini
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) directly as decision-making policies due to high cost and brittleness.
The proposed framework, SAGE (Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy), learns an autonomous policy from an imperfect but informative VLM teacher.
SAGE optimizes VLM usage by querying the teacher only when the learning agent exhibits uncertainty.

stories.title: Gradient-Update Mismatch: Rethinking Conflict-Free Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
stories.author: Tiejun Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses the 'Gradient-Update Mismatch' problem in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) where optimizing physics residuals and boundary conditions creates conflicting gradients.
It introduces 'gradient surgery' methods to construct conflict-free directions from loss-specific gradients to reduce training conflicts.
A key finding is that the conflict-free property achieved by gradient surgery may not be maintained after standard optimizer transformations.

stories.title: Can LLMs Discover Scientific Laws in Real and Parallel Worlds?
stories.author: Jingbo Shang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover fundamental scientific laws.
It addresses the open question of how to rigorously evaluate an LLM's genuine ability to perform scientific discovery.
Current evaluation methods are criticized for either using simplified synthetic environments or relying on pre-existing published knowledge.

stories.title: A Mathematical Theory of Reusable Neural Bases for Network Compression
stories.author: Binshuai Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the critical memory bottleneck in large AI models during training and inference.
Introduces the Linear Reusable Neural Bases Architecture (LRNBA) for improved parameter efficiency.
The core concept involves representing network blocks as linear combinations of a shared set of bases, inspired by RNNs.

stories.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
stories.author: Ming Jiang
bullet_points: The paper investigates the internal mechanisms of LLM-as-a-Judge systems used to evaluate Natural Language Generation (NLG) quality.
It introduces an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy to mechanistically probe how LLMs assign ratings across Readability and Adequacy.
This research addresses the lack of understanding regarding how LLM evaluators function when used as automated scoring tools or training signals.

stories.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces PTA-IRT, a new framework for benchmarking software engineering (SWE) agents.
Addresses the high cost of evaluating SWE agents by moving beyond simple pass/fail metrics.
PTA-IRT is 'Trajectory-Aware,' meaning it analyzes *how* agents solve problems, not just the final outcome.

stories.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
stories.author: Dimitri Kachler
bullet_points: Introduces CordisBench, a new 1,200-question benchmark for testing language model reasoning.
Focuses on the complex lifecycle reasoning required when language models dynamically alter their own execution environment (agent harnesses).
Tests the ability of models to track dependency propagation and necessary cleanup across changing software components.

stories.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Sambit Sahu
bullet_points: Introduces Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) as a new paradigm where natural language serves as a primary feedback channel for language agents.
VRL allows agents to receive feedback conveying intent, preferences, and causal structure in a human-interpretable way.
The field is structured around two axes: when verbal feedback is applied in an agent's lifecycle and what aspects of the agent it modifies.

stories.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: StudentSim proposes using LLM-based student simulators to gather data on effective AI tutoring strategies.
Existing simulation methods are limited: state-tracking models lack explanatory depth, while LLM role-play lacks competence matching.
The research addresses the challenge of gathering sparse, slow, and costly data on personalized learning guidance.

stories.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
stories.author: Chin-Chia Hsu
bullet_points: The research proposes 'Proactive Thought Partners,' AI agents designed to offer customizable, high-level cognitive support during the writing process.
Current proactive tools are often limited to basic, generic assistance like autocomplete, highlighting a gap in current AI writing support.
The paper explores the design space for AI that can anticipate and assist writers across diverse cognitive tasks, from ideation to revision.

stories.title: Closing Cost-Quality Gap in Document VLMs: Difficulty-Aware Data Curation and Quality-Adjusted Deployment Economics
stories.author: Aleksandr Ivanov
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost and quality gap in extracting structured data from massive document volumes in regulated industries.
Introduces a deployed system utilizing a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Vision-Language Model (VLM) for document understanding.
The research focuses on balancing model performance (quality) with operational costs, overcoming limitations of current open-source VLMs.

stories.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs
stories.author: Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
bullet_points: Addresses the open problem of optimally dividing a fixed annotation budget between Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) during LLM post-training.
Moves beyond broad trend observations to characterize a principled framework for near-optimal SFT-RL budget allocation.
Investigates whether the optimal SFT-RL ratio remains consistent when scaling from small to large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
stories.author: tatersolid
bullet_points: The FBI is investigating a service that was reportedly selling over 153 million driver's licenses.
This indicates a significant data security and identity theft threat.
The story highlights the risks associated with large-scale personal data breaches.

stories.title: Execution Trees, Not More Logs: A Better Debugging Model for AI Agents
stories.author: raju_dandigam
bullet_points: Proposes 'Execution Trees' as an alternative to traditional flat logging for debugging AI agents.
Argues that flat logs are insufficient for pinpointing the root cause of failures in complex AI operations.
Addresses a critical need in AI development: improving observability and traceability within autonomous agents.

stories.title: The blast radius rule for AI coding
stories.author: indiecoredev
bullet_points: Proposes a risk-based framework for autonomous AI coding agents.
The decision-making criteria prioritize the cost/difficulty of undoing a mistake over task complexity.
Outlines a three-zone system with specific checks for different levels of AI autonomy.
